name: Power I
summary: Three backs in the backfield: fullback and tailback stacked, and the Z offset beside them. An extra runner and an extra blocker at the point of attack over the base I.
personnel: 11 players, 2 tight ends, quarterback, fullback, tailback, Z offset in the backfield
notes: The base I with the Z brought off the line and into the backfield, offset beside the fullback about two and a half yards to the strong side. Both ends are ON the line and the Z is OFF it, so we still have exactly seven on the line. Which side he offsets to is the strength call — Power I Right or Power I Left — and it is what decides where Power and Counter go.
coaching_notes: Three backs in the backfield means an extra runner and an extra blocker without adding anybody new — it is the same eleven kids as the base I with the Z moved off the line. Install it once the I is solid and the line rules come almost free.

The Z offsets to the strength side the call names — Power I Right or Power I Left. He leads to that side on Power and Toss; on Counter he is the misdirection, running his lead path while the ball goes back the other way. The defense cannot see which until the snap.
Count seven on the line every snap. With the Z clearly a yard and a half into the backfield this is a harder look to line up illegally than a tight alignment, but check it anyway.
The Z is a back now, not a receiver. He blocks and he fakes at the same speed — a coasted fake tells the defense which back has the ball.
